To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have improved predictions for the $t\overline{t}W^{\pm}$ production process at the LHC and the Tevatron by including resummation effects at the next-to-next-leading logarithmic (NNLL) accuracy.
we have performed the resummation of soft gluons in the threshold limit with the next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy for the $t\hat{t}W^{\pm}$ production at hadron collider.

we have calculated the next-to-leading-order soft function for the $t\hat{t}V$ production and have performed the resummation of threshold logarithms in $t\hat tV$ production at next-to-next-to leading logarithms (NNLL) accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the factorization and the resummation of threshold corrections to the $t\overline{t} W^\pm$ production.
the resummation of threshold logarithms in the production of $t\bar t W^\pm$ at the LHC.
the study of the production of top quarks at hadron collators, in particular, the $t\hat{t}W^+$ process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resummed N$^2$LL calculation is a good approximation to the full NNLO QCD calculation for the $t\overline{t}$ production in the threshold region.
the resummated N$^2$LL results are in good agreement with the NLO QCD predictions, but they are more precise and stable.
the resummative calculation with NNNLL accuracy is a good approximation to the cross section at hadron collider.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resummated cross section is more stable against the variation of scales and the resummation effect is significant for the $t\overline{t}W^{\pm}$ production at the LHC and the HL-LHC.
the resummations are necessary and important to improve the precision of the cross section predictions at hadron collidors.
the $t\overline{t}W^{\pm}$ production is a promising process for the measurement of the top quark Yukawa coupling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resummations of the large logarithms are important for the $t\overline{t}W$ production at hadronic colliders.
the resummed cross section is much more scale-stable than the NLO cross section.
, in the threshold region, the resummation effect is significant and the NLL accuracy is necessary for a precise prediction of this important process.
